newsitem.title: FRANCE: TENNIS-KAFELNIKOV, HENMAN GO THROUGH TO SEMIFINAL CLASH.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-KAFELNIKOV, HENMAN GO THROUGH TO SEMIFINAL CLASH.

text.p: Russian Yevgeny Kafelnikov will be seeking revenge for his Wimbledon defeat by Tim Henman when he meets the Briton in the semifinals of the Lyon Grand Prix on Saturday.
The number two seed beat Swede Magnus Gustafsson 5-7 7-5 6-3 in their quarter-final on Friday to set up the clash with Henman, 7-6 6-2 winner over Karol Kucera of Slovakia.
"It was very tight throughout the match and Magnus really put me through a lot of work," said the French Open champion and world number four.
"He dictated play during the first two sets even though I managed to win the second. And in the third he always had me under pressure."
Kafelnikov, the highest surviving seed after the elimination of Austrian Thomas Muster, will be pleased to know he can raise his game when necessary as he prepares to face Henman.
The Briton, who upset Kafelnikov in the first round at Wimbledon and went on to reach the quarter-finals, had an easier time against Kucera.

Once he had the first set in the bag following a tough tiebreak that went to 8-6, Henman ran away with the match despite being kept on court for two and a half hours by Dutchman Jan Siemerink in their late second round match on Thursday.

"After my long and testing match on Thursday I was tired. But I slept well and despite blisters which appeared this morning during practice it went well," said Henman, who is looking to reach his first ATP Tour tournament final.
"I knew that against Kucera I was going to have to run a lot and stand up to his service and I was ready."
Henman, speaking before he knew the identity of his semifinal opponent, added: "I've already beaten both so why not again."
